newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai to exceed 1997 GDP growth goal of 10 pct.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai to exceed 1997 GDP growth goal of 10 pct.

text.p: The economy of China's richest city and its financial hub roared ahead in the first half of 1997 and looks set to exceed official targets to record growth of up to 13 percent for the year, an official said on Thursday.

The city had set a target for 10 percent growth in gross domestic product (GDP) for 1997, and had already recorded a first-half increase of 13.7 percent to around 154.36 billion yuan, said Wu Zhenguo, deputy director of the Shanghai municipal statistics bureau.
"Our view is that we will definitely reach our original target of a 10 percent increase (in GDP) this year," said Wu.
"We think there is a foundation for exceeding 12 percent and it is possible GDP growth will reach 13 percent with effort," he told reporters at a briefing.
City officials in February set a goal of 10 percent GDP growth for 1997.
But Wu said exceeding the set target was normal given Shanghai's position as China's financial centre, and it would have no negative fallout on the city's economy.
"There won't be any negative effect," he said. "Under the demands of the whole country, Shanghai's economic development must be faster than other cities."
"We are China's most developed city so the speed of economic development must be faster," Wu said.
Despite the fast economic growth, inflation was relatively low in the first half of 1997, he said.
Consumer prices rose 2.8 percent in January-June compared with the same period in 1996, Wu said.
Retail prices, a narrower measure of inflation that excludes services, fell 0.3 percent, he said.
However, the economy was not without its trouble spots.
Fixed asset investment slowed sharply in the first half of 1997 due to a fall in property investment and less investment by the central government in large Shanghai enterprises, Wu said.
Investment in fixed assets was about 55.79 billion yuan in the first six months, up 4.5 percent from the same period last year but representing a 42.9 percentage point slowdown in growth, he said.
"We estimate we will still be able to meet our target for fixed asset investment," Wu said, adding the target for 1997 was 220 billion yuan.
